claim: Prrx1 genetically marks all auricular chondrocytes in adult mice.
source: Genetic tracing experiments showed that Prrx1 marks all chondrocytes in the auricle.
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 1A demonstrating Prrx1 labeling of auricle chondrocytes.

claim: Prrx1 marks very few chondrocytes in the growth plates and articular cartilages in adult mice.
source: This finding is in contrast to the labeling of very small populations of chondrocytes in the growth plates and articular cartilages (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Prrx1 marks dermal cells in the skin of the ear in adult mice.
source: As expected, Prrx1 also marked dermal cells in the skin of the ear in adult mice (Figure 1A); we previously showed that Prrx1 marks CD31-CD45-CD200+CD51+ dermal stem cells (Liu et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data in Figure 1A and previous publication by Liu et al., 2022.

claim: Auricle chondrocytes do not express Vimentin or Col1α1/2.
source: Immunostaining results showed that auricle chondrocytes did not express Vimentin or Col1α1/2, which were mainly expressed in the dermis of the ear, or Col2 or Col10 (Figure 1C and data not shown).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: αSMA is mainly expressed in the smooth muscle of blood vessels in the ear.
source: Moreover, αSMA is mainly expressed in the smooth muscle of blood vessels (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Auricle chondrocytes were Tomato+ when TAM was given at E8.5, E13.5, or p21.
source: We found that auricle chondrocytes were Tomato+ under these conditions even only one dose of TAM (1/10 of the dose for adult mice) was given to the pregnant mice at E8.5 or E13.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: E8.5 mice showed Tomato+ chondrocytes at both articular cartilage and growth plate.
source: However, while E8.5 mice showed Tomato+ chondrocytes at both articular cartilage and growth plate, E13.5 or p21 mice showed much fewer Tomato+ chondrocytes at articular cartilage and growth plate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: E13.5 or p21 mice showed much fewer Tomato+ chondrocytes at articular cartilage and growth plate compared to E8.5 mice.
source: However, while E8.5 mice showed Tomato+ chondrocytes at both articular cartilage and growth plate, E13.5 or p21 mice showed much fewer Tomato+ chondrocytes at articular cartilage and growth plate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Prrx1 expression differs in cartilages during development, growth, and maintenance.
source: These results indicate that Prrx1 expression differs in cartilages during development, growth, and maintenance.
evidence: Inferred from the differential labeling patterns at different developmental stages shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ablation of Bmpr1a in Prrx1+ cells in adult mice led to a decrease in p-Smad1/5/9 in the ear.
source: We observed a decrease in p-Smad1/5/9 on the ear sections of the Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice 60 days after TAM administration while the protein levels were not affected (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A and Western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: qPCR analysis confirmed the ablation of Bmpr1a in the auricle cartilage of Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: qPCR analysis confirmed the ablation of Bmpr1a in the auricle cartilage (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The size and body weight of Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice were slightly reduced.
source: Note that the size and body weight of Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice were slightly reduced (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice showed a quick decrease in the size of the external ear.
source: Interestingly, the mice showed a quick decrease in the size of the external ear (Figure 2C), indicating a problem with auricle cartilage, which provides strength for the ear.
evidence: Supported by measurements and images shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The ear phenotype in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice mainly occurred at the distal part of the ear.
source: Histological analysis showed that the phenotype mainly occurred at the distal part of the ear.
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The thickness of the cartilage was slightly reduced in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: The thickness of the cartilage was slightly reduced, associated with a great reduction in the cell size (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by histological measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Cell size was greatly reduced in the auricle cartilage of Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: The thickness of the cartilage was slightly reduced, associated with a great reduction in the cell size (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by histological measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There was no difference in the number of proliferating cells between the mutant and control mice.
source: Staining for Ki67 showed that there was no difference in the number of proliferating cells between the mutant and control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by Ki67 staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: There were very few proliferating cells in the mutant or control mice.
source: Note that there were very few proliferating cells in the mutant or control mice.
evidence: Observation from Ki67 staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Chondrocytes did not undergo apoptosis in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: Staining for apoptotic cells indicated that chondrocytes did not undergo apoptosis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by TUNEL staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The ear phenotype observed in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice is not due to decreases in the number of chondrocytes via altered proliferation and/or apoptosis.
source: Overall, these results suggest that the ear phenotype observed in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice is not due to decreases in the number of chondrocytes via altered proliferation and/or apoptosis; rather, it occurs through shrinkage of chondrocytes.
evidence: Inferred from Ki67 and TUNEL staining data showing no changes in proliferation or apoptosis.

claim: The ear phenotype in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice occurs through shrinkage of chondrocytes.
source: Overall, these results suggest that the ear phenotype observed in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice is not due to decreases in the number of chondrocytes via altered proliferation and/or apoptosis; rather, it occurs through shrinkage of chondrocytes.
evidence: Inferred from the observation of reduced cell size without changes in cell number.

claim: Deletion of Prrx1 and Prrx2 led to microtia development.
source: Interestingly, deletion of Prrx1 and its paralog gene Prrx2 led to microtia development, while deletion of Prrx1 leads to low-set ears and deletion of Prrx2 does not affect ear development (Martin et al., 1995; ten Berge et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Martin et al., 1995 and ten Berge et al., 1998.

claim: Deletion of Prrx1 leads to low-set ears.
source: Interestingly, deletion of Prrx1 and its paralog gene Prrx2 led to microtia development, while deletion of Prrx1 leads to low-set ears and deletion of Prrx2 does not affect ear development (Martin et al., 1995; ten Berge et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Martin et al., 1995 and ten Berge et al., 1998.

claim: Deletion of Prrx2 does not affect ear development.
source: Interestingly, deletion of Prrx1 and its paralog gene Prrx2 led to microtia development, while deletion of Prrx1 leads to low-set ears and deletion of Prrx2 does not affect ear development (Martin et al., 1995; ten Berge et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Martin et al., 1995 and ten Berge et al., 1998.

claim: Prrx1 and Prrx2 play a redundant role in external ear development.
source: These results suggest that these two genes play a redundant role in external ear development.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that deletion of both genes causes microtia while deletion of individual genes has milder or no effects.

claim: No ear phenotype was observed in Prrx1CreERT mice (with one Prrx1 allele deleted).
source: However, we found no ear phenotype in Prrx1CreERT (with one Prrx1 allele deleted) or Bmpr1af/f mice compared to wild-type mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C), suggesting that ablation of one copy of Prrx1 does not affect ear maintenance.
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: No ear phenotype was observed in Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: However, we found no ear phenotype in Prrx1CreERT (with one Prrx1 allele deleted) or Bmpr1af/f mice compared to wild-type mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C), suggesting that ablation of one copy of Prrx1 does not affect ear maintenance.
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Ablation of one copy of Prrx1 does not affect ear maintenance.
source: However, we found no ear phenotype in Prrx1CreERT (with one Prrx1 allele deleted) or Bmpr1af/f mice compared to wild-type mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C), suggesting that ablation of one copy of Prrx1 does not affect ear maintenance.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of phenotype in Prrx1CreERT mice shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The growth plate appeared normal in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: The growth plate and the articular cartilage appeared to be normal in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B), likely due to the lack of labeling of chondrocytes at these locations.
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The articular cartilage appeared normal in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: The growth plate and the articular cartilage appeared to be normal in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B), likely due to the lack of labeling of chondrocytes at these locations.
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The normal appearance of growth plate and articular cartilage in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice is likely due to the lack of labeling of chondrocytes at these locations.
source: The growth plate and the articular cartilage appeared to be normal in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B), likely due to the lack of labeling of chondrocytes at these locations.
evidence: Inferred from the lineage tracing data showing minimal labeling in these locations.

claim: Smad1/5/9 is activated in proliferating chondrocytes but not hypertrophic chondrocytes in the growth plate.
source: Moreover, Smad1/5/9 is reportedly activated in proliferating chondrocytes but not hypertrophic chondrocytes in the growth plate (Retting et al., 2009; Yoon et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Retting et al., 2009 and Yoon et al., 2006.

claim: BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling is more active at the distal part than at the proximal or middle part of the auricle in young or old mice.
source: Our immunostaining of p-Smad1/5/9 results revealed that BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling is more active at the distal part than at the proximal or middle part, in young or old mice (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A.

claim: BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling was activated to a greater extent at the distal part of the auricle compared to proximal and middle parts.
source: We found that BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling was activated to a greater extent at the distal part of the auricle (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: Supported by Western blot analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The injury at the distal or middle part of the auricle could not be repaired after 4 weeks.
source: It was clear that the injury at the distal or middle part could not be repaired, while the injury at the proximal part was repaired (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C and D).
evidence: Supported by cartilage regeneration assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C and D.

claim: The injury at the proximal part of the auricle was repaired after 4 weeks.
source: It was clear that the injury at the distal or middle part could not be repaired, while the injury at the proximal part was repaired (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C and D).
evidence: Supported by cartilage regeneration assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C and D.

claim: Chondrocytes at the distal part of the auricle have the lowest regenerative activity.
source: These results suggest that chondrocytes at the distal part of the auricle have the lowest regenerative activity and thus may be the most differentiated, which is associated with the strongest activation of BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the regeneration assay data showing lack of repair at the distal part.

claim: Chondrocytes at the distal part of the auricle may be the most differentiated.
source: These results suggest that chondrocytes at the distal part of the auricle have the lowest regenerative activity and thus may be the most differentiated, which is associated with the strongest activation of BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between low regenerative activity and high BMP signaling at the distal part.

claim: The lowest regenerative activity at the distal part is associated with the strongest activation of BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling.
source: These results suggest that chondrocytes at the distal part of the auricle have the lowest regenerative activity and thus may be the most differentiated, which is associated with the strongest activation of BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between regenerative capacity and BMP signaling levels shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Col1a2 marked dermal cells but not auricle chondrocytes in Col1a2-CreERT; Rosa26LSL-tdTomato mice.
source: We found that Col1a2 marked dermal cells but not auricle chondrocytes in Col1a2-CreERT; Rosa26LSL-tdTomato mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5A.

claim: The levels of p-Smad1/5/9 in the dermis were greatly reduced in dermal cells in Col1a2-CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: Immunostaining results showed that the levels of p-Smad1/5/9 in the dermis were greatly reduced in dermal cells in the mutant mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5B.

claim: qPCR analysis confirmed the ablation of Bmpr1a in the dermal cells of Col1a2-CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: qPCR analysis confirmed the ablation of Bmpr1a in the dermal cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5C.

claim: The ears appeared normal in Col1a2-CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice 6 months after TAM injection.
source: The ears appeared normal in Col1a2-CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice 6 months after TAM injection (Figure 2—figure supplement 5D and E).
evidence: Supported by phenotypic and histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5D and E.

claim: Acta2 could mark a small portion of chondrocytes in the middle segment of the auricle and smooth muscle cells of the blood vessels.
source: In addition, we traced the Acta2 (encoding αSMA) lineage cells in auricles and found that Acta2 could mark a small portion of chondrocytes in the middle segment of the auricle and smooth muscle cells of the blood vessels (Figure 2—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: Supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6A.

claim: Ablation of Bmpr1a in Acta2+ cells did not produce an ear phenotype.
source: We also generated Acta2-CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice and found that ablation of Bmpr1a in Acta2+ did not produce an ear phenotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 6B–6E).
evidence: Supported by phenotypic and histological analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6B–6E.

claim: BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling affects ear maintenance via its effect on chondrocytes at the distal segment, with little contribution from dermal cells or smooth muscle cells.
source: These findings suggest that BMP-Smad1/5/9 signaling affects ear maintenance via its effect on chondrocytes at the distal segment, with little contribution from dermal cells or smooth muscle cells.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of phenotype when Bmpr1a is ablated in dermal cells or smooth muscle cells.

claim: Ablation of Bmpr1a in Prrx1+ cells in young mice (P21) led to a decrease in p-Smad1/5/9 in the ear.
source: We observed a decrease in p-Smad1/5/9 on the ear sections of the Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: qPCR analysis confirmed the ablation of Bmpr1a in the auricle cartilage of young Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: qPCR analysis confirmed the ablation of Bmpr1a in the auricle cartilage (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Young Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice showed decreases in the ear size.
source: We found decreases in the ear size and the volumes of chondrocytes at the distal part of the ear in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: Supported by measurements shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Young Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice showed decreases in the volumes of chondrocytes at the distal part of the ear.
source: We found decreases in the ear size and the volumes of chondrocytes at the distal part of the ear in Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: Supported by measurements shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Young Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice showed normal growth plates and articular cartilage.
source: However, these mice showed normal growth plates and articular cartilage (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), likely attributable to the lack of labeling of chondrocytes in the growth plate and articular cartilage in Prrx1CreERT; Rosa26LSL-tdTomato mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: BMP signaling is required for both growth and maintenance of the auricle.
source: Overall, these results suggest that BMP signaling is required for both growth and maintenance of the auricle.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that Bmpr1a ablation causes microtia in both young and adult mice.

claim: The transcription of at least 500 genes was affected by Bmpr1a ablation in the auricle.
source: We found that the transcription of at least 500 genes was affected by Bmpr1a ablation (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Bmpr1a ablation led to increased expression of genes in inflammation.
source: KEGG and GO analyses revealed that Bmpr1a ablation led to increased expression of genes in inflammation, stemness, cell cycle, mesenchymal cell development, proximal/distal patterning, ear morphogenesis, wound healing, TGFβ signaling, and PKA signaling, whereas genes in chondrocyte differentiation, stem cell division, skeletal morphogenesis, extracellular matrix (ECM) genes, cartilage development, Hedgehog signaling, and Wnt signaling were suppressed (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: Supported by KEGG and GO analysis shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Bmpr1a ablation led to increased expression of genes in stemness.
source: KEGG and GO analyses revealed that Bmpr1a ablation led to increased expression of genes in inflammation, stemness, cell cycle, mesenchymal cell development, proximal/distal patterning, ear morphogenesis, wound healing, TGFβ signaling, and PKA signaling, whereas genes in chondrocyte differentiation, stem cell division, skeletal morphogenesis, extracellular matrix (ECM) genes, cartilage development, Hedgehog signaling, and Wnt signaling were suppressed (Figure 4B and C).

claim: Bmpr1a ablation may cause chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transformation.
source: These transcriptome results suggest that Bmpr1a ablation may cause chondrocyte-to-osteoblast transformation.
evidence: Inferred from the transcriptome changes showing increased osteoblast-related genes and decreased chondrocyte-related genes.

claim: The expression of many ECM proteins was down-regulated in the auricle cartilage of Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice.
source: Further analysis showed that the expression of many ECM proteins was down-regulated in the auricle cartilage of Prrx1CreERT; Bmpr1af/f mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by heatmap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: mRNA levels of Smad1/5/9 were unaltered in the auricle cartilage of the mutant mice.
source: Note that mRNA levels of Smad1/5/9 were unaltered in the auricle cartilage of the mutant mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by FPKM values shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The expression of aggrecan in the growth plates was unaltered in the mutant mice.
source: Immunostaining revealed that the expression of aggrecan and Col10 in the growth plates was unaltered in the mutant mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), likely due to the lack of marking of growth plate chondrocytes by Prrx1 in adult mice.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The expression of Col10 in the growth plates was unaltered in the mutant mice.
source: Immunostaining revealed that the expression of aggrecan and Col10 in the growth plates was unaltered in the mutant mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), likely due to the lack of marking of growth plate chondrocytes by Prrx1 in adult mice.
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Some protein trafficking genes were up-regulated in Bmpr1a-deficient auricle cartilage.
source: Since ECM proteins are secreted by chondrocytes, we also checked the expression of proteins involved in protein trafficking and found that some were up-regulated and some were down-regulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by heatmap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Some protein trafficking genes were down-regulated in Bmpr1a-deficient auricle cartilage.
source: Since ECM proteins are secreted by chondrocytes, we also checked the expression of proteins involved in protein trafficking and found that some were up-regulated and some were down-regulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by heatmap analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The expression of ER stress-related genes was not altered by Bmpr1a ablation.
source: However, the expression of ER or Golgi stress-related genes, which play critical roles in chondrocyte differentiation and survival (Horigome et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018), was not altered by Bmpr1a ablation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: Supported by FPKM values shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The expression of Golgi stress-related genes was not altered by Bmpr1a ablation.
source: However, the expression of ER or Golgi stress-related genes, which play critical roles in chondrocyte differentiation and survival (Horigome et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018), was not altered by Bmpr1a ablation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E and F).

claim: Microtia causes hearing problems and delays in language learning.
